numbers.source: a 26 x 1 3/8 inch roadster tyre: 590 mm bead seat plus two 35 mm sections is about 660 (the ISO number is from memory: not reached on a page this session); error 10
a gent's roadster's wheelbase is about 1100 to 1140; from the stated tube lengths and angles: 1097; error 40
a rider of 1.75 m sits with the saddle about 1.0 m up; error 40
roadster bars stand about as high as the saddle or just above it; error 40
a roadster's bottom bracket is about 300 mm up (30 mm below the axles); error 15
swept-back roadster bars are 560 to 620 between the bends and about 790 over the grips' ends; error 50
the review of 13 October: an 18 tooth sprocket 73 mm across (12.7 pitch: pitch circle 73.2); S1 shows a rusted wheel in which no sprocket reads; error 3
the review: sheet steel 60 deep, 1 thick; no chainguard reads in S1; error 5
the review: rims 25 wide, 10 deep, as their own ring (a 26 x 1 3/8 steel rim is about 22 to 25 wide); S1's rims read as thin rings; error 3
the review: a 340 x 130 platform of 10 mm tube at 780 over the rear wheel; S1's own row lists a rear carrier but at 430 px no number reads; error 20

sources.author: Jeremy Bolwell
sources.shows: a rusted gent's roadster leaning on a stone wall in a ruined building: a diamond frame with a level top tube, two big spoked wheels with mudguards, swept-back bars, a sprung saddle, a rear carrier; the rear wheel nearer the camera so the perspective is strong
sources.not_used_for: any number (the camera is oblique and close, the picture low in contrast); the rust is a wear state, not the sample's; the layout of the missing parts (no brake rod, chain or carrier reads in the 430 px crop, a rusted dark machine)
sources.period: 2012, and an INTERIOR: the machine rests in a ruined chapel room, on its page 'maybe 50 years' (the Pant y Celyn Baptist ruin), so it dates the type, a roadster of the 1950s or before, not the street; the roadster for 1990 stays a Judgement (an older rider's bicycle, plausible in a port town); the alternative, named and not written, is a 1980s utility frame (a town bicycle on 26 x 1 3/8 wheels with cable callipers and a rear rack)

sources.author: DS Pugh
sources.shows: a modern road bicycle leaning with its front tyre against a dry-stone wall: shows how a bicycle leans on a wall (front wheel and bar end against the stone, the rear wheel on the ground at a lean of about 10 to 15 degrees); a pannier and a bottle (brands masked)
sources.not_used_for: the bicycle's form (modern: 700c wheels, derailleur, drop frame) and any number

night.note: the bicycle stands against the blank wall between lamp pools; the chrome catches the lantern colour (1.0, 0.25, 0.0) as thin glints on the rims and bars, the black frame vanishes

placement.slot: west side, against the soot-brick wall of the west_south block (the plain ground floor: no shopfront), the bicycle parallel to the wall facing +x (up the street), its LEFT grip end touching the brick, leaning 12 degrees toward the wall (the first version leaned it away from the wall: the wall stood on the side the top tips away from), its tyres 0.60 m from the wall at the ground; the rear tyre's back at x 14.12, the front tyre's front at x 15.88 (centre x 15.0), the grip's contact at x 15.15 on brick between the cottage door at x 13.5 (the doorstep to x 14.0) and the cottage window at x 15.9 (its sill from x 15.425); the wall at z -5.125

openings_named.source: the DRAWN street: terrace-front.py's plain-row rule (a household door at bay start + 1.5 m, windows at + 3.3 and + 5.1, the west rows turned: street x = the bay's high end less the local x), as the front-doors-all target (street.houses) and the house-windows target (sites) list them; the scene file's own coarse boxes put a door at x 16.5 and a window at x 14.1 (vignette-pieces.json west_south_door2), which the drawn street does not use

reasons: the soot-brick wall of the cottages is where small things lean (the poster wall of the scene, x 11.4); it is NOT blank at x 14.1 to 15.9: the drawn plain row has a household door at x 13.5 (opening 13.08 to 13.92, a doorstep 0.998 wide and 0.35 m deep to x 14.0), a cottage window at x 15.9 (opening 15.475 to 16.325, sill 0.82 m above the crown, its stone sill 50 mm proud from x 15.425) and another at x 17.7; the first version's 'no door (the side door is at x 25.5)' read x 25.5 on the west_north block and missed all of it

the slot keeps the grip's contact on brick: the left grip's end touches the wall at x 15.15, 0.28 m from the window's sill and 1.15 m from the doorstep's edge; both tyres stand clear of the door: the rear tyre's back (x 14.12) is 0.2 m past the door's approach (x 13.92) and 0.12 m past the doorstep's end (x 14.0), and the tyres stand 0.6 m out, 0.25 m beyond the step's front edge (0.35 m)

leaning, it takes a footway depth of its roll: a 12 degree lean puts the left grip end 0.60 m from the tyres' line and the right pedal and grip 0.18 m on the other side, so the bicycle takes 0.78 m of the 2.0 m footway and leaves 1.22 m clear on the kerb side (the first version's 0.34 m and 1.64 m came from the same wall on the wrong side)
it is an adult's bicycle, ambient dressing that belongs to no one on the street's list of residents

wear: enamel chipped to red-brown rust at the dropouts, the head tube's lower end, the seat-stay bridge and the mudguard stays; paint dulled, a few small dents in the mudguards
chrome gone to dull grey with orange pitting on the bars, rims and spokes; the chain brown with oil and rust, a line of oil spots below the lower run
tyres hard, cracked at the sidewalls, one slightly soft (flat at the ground by 8 mm: a seed), grey dust bloom
the saddle cracked and shiny at the nose; the grips worn smooth at their ends
a wet street under it: darkness on the lowest 150 mm of the tyres and a grit splash on the mudguard
NOT shown: a lock or chain bar (a chain through the wheel is a variant, a seed), a basket, stabilisers, any maker's badge on the head tube (a real bicycle has one; this has a blank plate)

variants_note: BI2 (the sample): the roadster leaning 12 degrees toward the wall, its left grip end against the brick.
BI1: the same upright (for a bicycle held by a figure or standing on a stand).
a ten-speed with drop bars is the second kind of adult bicycle of 1990: not written (its frame would be a new target); one kind only, as the street needs one bicycle.
conditions (materials): C0 sound, C1 worn (the sample's wear), C2 rusted solid (S1's state, a derelict leaning for years).
not_settled: no 1975 to 1995 bicycle photograph was measurable and S1 and S2 are oblique and low in contrast: every number is Judgement (a gent's roadster's usual geometry), checked for internal consistency and against ranges, not against pixels
the 26 x 1 3/8 wheel's exact tyre diameter (660 mm is from memory; the page that gives the ISO 590 bead seat was not reached)
whether the street's bicycle should be a roadster or a ten-speed (the roadster is chosen because S1 is a street-leaning roadster)

added after the review of 13 October (each a Judgement from its list, none readable in S1 or S3 at the size they are seen): the chain on its pitch circles, the 18 tooth sprocket, the chainguard, the rims as their own ring, rod brakes (two 120 mm levers, two 8 mm rods, a stirrup under each rim), two 5 mm stays on each mudguard, the 340 x 130 carrier at 780 and the 60 mm red reflector; the lamp is not modelled (a dynamo lamp, a texture and decal if wanted); the chain's links are lumped in strips (each says how many links it stands for)

the brake type: rod brakes with stirrups under the rims are the review's first choice and fit a roadster; side-pull callipers with a 60 mm reach are the cable alternative (a 1980s town bicycle) and are not written
the lean's wall contact is by the left grip end (S2 shows the front tyre against the wall): either is a seed
content_rule_note: an adult's bicycle only: no small frame, no stabilisers, no child seat, no toy (a statement of the content rule).
builder_notes: build by script: the tubes as cylinders from the end points in target.json (a part's p0 and p1), the tyres as one torus of section 38 (the 16 boxes are the engine's approximation), the 36 spokes (8 drawn) in the real wheel; the mudguards as one swept strip per wheel
BI2 is BI1 with the part transform (a roll of 12 degrees about the x axis through the tyre contacts) and the wall; the builder places the bicycle with the transform
no maker's badge, no transfer, no lettering of any kind

the left grip end is the point that touches the wall (the lean tips the top toward -y, the rider's left; the first version put the wall on the other side); stand the sample at the pose in target.json (yaw 0, x 14.45, z from the wall less the grip's reach)

the chain: strips of 8 x 6 mm on the pitch circles (88.9 and 36.6 radius) joined by two runs on the common tangents; build real links of 12.7 pitch along the same path (102 links); the chain, ring and sprocket lie in the plane y = 55, outboard of the chain stays at y = +-40
